name: SET
summary: Set the string value of a key
syntax: SET key value [NX | XX] [GET] [EX seconds | PX milliseconds | KEEPTTL]

name: GET
summary: Get the value of a key

name: SETNX
summary: Set the value of a key, only if the key does not exist

name: SETEX
summary: Set the value and expiration of a key

name: PSETEX
summary: Set the value and expiration in milliseconds of a key

name: MGET
summary: Get the values of all given keys
complexity: O(N) where N is the number of keys

name: MSET
summary: Set multiple keys to multiple values atomically
complexity: O(N) where N is the number of keys

name: MSETNX
summary: Set multiple keys only if none of the keys exist
complexity: O(N) where N is the number of keys

name: INCR
summary: Increment the integer value of a key by one

name: DECR
summary: Decrement the integer value of a key by one

name: INCRBY
summary: Increment the integer value of a key by the given amount

name: DECRBY
summary: Decrement the integer value of a key by the given number

name: INCRBYFLOAT
summary: Increment the float value of a key by the given amount

name: APPEND
summary: Append a value to a key

name: STRLEN
summary: Get the length of the value stored in a key

name: GETRANGE
summary: Get a substring of the string stored at a key
complexity: O(N) where N is the length of returned string

name: SETRANGE
summary: Overwrite part of a string at key starting at the specified offset

name: GETSET
summary: Atomically set key to value and return the old value

name: GETDEL
summary: Get the value of a key and delete the key

name: GETEX
summary: Get the value of a key and optionally set its expiration
syntax: GETEX key [EX seconds | PX milliseconds | PERSIST]

name: LCS
summary: Find longest common substring between two keys
complexity: O(N*M) where N and M are string lengths

name: LPUSH
summary: Prepend one or multiple elements to a list

name: RPUSH
summary: Append one or multiple elements to a list

name: LPUSHX
summary: Prepend an element to a list, only if the list exists

name: RPUSHX
summary: Append an element to a list, only if the list exists

name: LPOP
summary: Remove and return the first element(s) of a list
complexity: O(N) where N is the number of elements returned

name: RPOP
summary: Remove and return the last element(s) of a list
complexity: O(N) where N is the number of elements returned

name: LRANGE
summary: Get a range of elements from a list
complexity: O(S+N) where S is start offset and N is range length

name: LLEN
summary: Get the length of a list

name: LINDEX
summary: Get an element from a list by its index
complexity: O(N) where N is index distance from head or tail

name: LSET
summary: Set the value of an element in a list by its index
complexity: O(N) where N is index distance

name: LREM
summary: Remove elements from a list matching value
complexity: O(N+M) where N is list length

name: LTRIM
summary: Trim a list to the specified range
complexity: O(N) where N is number of removed elements

name: RPOPLPUSH
summary: Atomically return the last element of a list and push it to another

name: LMOVE
summary: Atomically move an element from one list to another

name: BLPOP
summary: Blocking version of LPOP waiting until an element is available
complexity: O(N) where N is number of keys

name: BRPOP
summary: Blocking version of RPOP waiting until an element is available
complexity: O(N) where N is number of keys

name: LPOS
summary: Return the index of matching elements in a list
syntax: LPOS key element [RANK rank] [COUNT num-matches] [MAXLEN len]
complexity: O(N) where N is list length

name: HSET
summary: Set the string value of a hash field

name: HGET
summary: Get the value of a hash field

name: HMSET
summary: Set multiple hash fields to multiple values
complexity: O(N) where N is the number of fields

name: HMGET
summary: Get the values of all the given hash fields
complexity: O(N) where N is number of fields

name: HGETALL
summary: Get all the fields and values in a hash
complexity: O(N) where N is the size of the hash

name: HDEL
summary: Delete one or more hash fields
complexity: O(N) where N is number of fields to remove

name: HEXISTS
summary: Determine if a hash field exists

name: HLEN
summary: Get the number of fields in a hash

name: HKEYS
summary: Get all the fields in a hash
complexity: O(N) where N is size of hash

name: HVALS
summary: Get all the values in a hash
complexity: O(N) where N is size of hash

name: HINCRBY
summary: Increment the integer value of a hash field by the given number

name: HINCRBYFLOAT
summary: Increment the float value of a hash field by the given amount

name: HSETNX
summary: Set the value of a hash field, only if the field does not exist

name: HSCAN
summary: Incrementally iterate hash fields and associated values
complexity: O(1) for every call; O(N) for complete iteration

name: HRANDFIELD
summary: Get one or multiple random fields from a hash
complexity: O(N) where N is number of fields requested

name: HSTRLEN
summary: Get the string length of the value of a hash field

name: SADD
summary: Add one or more members to a set

name: SREM
summary: Remove one or more members from a set
complexity: O(N) where N is number of members to remove

name: SMEMBERS
summary: Get all the members in a set
complexity: O(N) where N is the set cardinality

name: SISMEMBER
summary: Determine if a given value is a member of a set

name: SMISMEMBER
summary: Check if multiple members exist in a set
complexity: O(N) where N is number of members checked

name: SCARD
summary: Get the number of members in a set

name: SPOP
summary: Remove and return one or multiple random members from a set

name: SRANDMEMBER
summary: Get one or multiple random members from a set without removing

name: SINTER
summary: Intersect multiple sets and return the members
complexity: O(N*M) worst case where N is cardinality of smallest set

name: SUNION
summary: Add multiple sets and return the members
complexity: O(N) where N is total number of elements in all sets

name: SDIFF
summary: Subtract multiple sets and return the members
complexity: O(N) where N is total number of elements

name: SINTERSTORE
summary: Intersect multiple sets and store the resulting set in a key

name: SUNIONSTORE
summary: Add multiple sets and store the resulting set in a key
complexity: O(N) where N is total elements

name: SDIFFSTORE
summary: Subtract multiple sets and store the resulting set in a key
complexity: O(N) where N is total elements

name: SSCAN
summary: Incrementally iterate set elements

name: SMOVE
summary: Move a member from one set to another atomically

name: ZADD
summary: Add one or more members to a sorted set, or update its score if it already exists
syntax: ZADD key [NX | XX] [GT | LT] [CH] [INCR] score member [score member ...]

name: ZREM
summary: Remove one or more members from a sorted set
complexity: O(M*log(N)) where M is number of members removed

name: ZSCORE
summary: Get the score associated with the given member in a sorted set

name: ZMSCORE
summary: Get the scores associated with multiple members in a sorted set
complexity: O(N) where N is number of members checked

name: ZRANK
summary: Determine the index of a member in a sorted set, with scores ordered from low to high

name: ZREVRANK
summary: Determine the index of a member in a sorted set, with scores ordered from high to low

name: ZCARD
summary: Get the number of members in a sorted set

name: ZCOUNT
summary: Count the members in a sorted set with scores within the given values

name: ZRANGE
summary: Return a range of members in a sorted set
syntax: ZRANGE key min max [BYSCORE | BYLEX] [REV] [LIMIT offset count] [WITHSCORES]

name: ZREVRANGE
summary: Return a range of members in a sorted set, by index, with scores ordered from high to low

name: ZRANGEBYSCORE
summary: Return a range of members in a sorted set, by score
syntax: ZRANGEBYSCORE key min max [WITHSCORES] [LIMIT offset count]

name: ZREVRANGEBYSCORE
summary: Return a range of members in a sorted set, by score, ordered from high to low
syntax: ZREVRANGEBYSCORE key max min [WITHSCORES] [LIMIT offset count]

name: ZINCRBY
summary: Increment the score of a member in a sorted set

name: ZPOPMIN
summary: Remove and return members with the lowest scores in a sorted set

name: ZPOPMAX
summary: Remove and return members with the highest scores in a sorted set

name: ZSCAN
summary: Incrementally iterate sorted sets elements and associated scores

name: ZREMRANGEBYRANK
summary: Remove all members in a sorted set within the given indexes

name: ZREMRANGEBYSCORE
summary: Remove all members in a sorted set within the given scores

name: ZLEXCOUNT
summary: Count the number of members in a sorted set between a given lexicographical range

name: DEL
summary: Delete one or more keys
complexity: O(N) where N is number of keys removed

name: UNLINK
summary: Delete one or more keys asynchronously in another background thread

name: EXISTS
summary: Determine if one or more keys exist
complexity: O(N) where N is number of keys checked

name: TYPE
summary: Determine the type stored at key

name: TTL
summary: Get the time to live for a key in seconds

name: PTTL
summary: Get the time to live for a key in milliseconds

name: EXPIRE
summary: Set a key's time to live in seconds
syntax: EXPIRE key seconds [NX | XX | GT | LT]

name: PEXPIRE
summary: Set a key's time to live in milliseconds
syntax: PEXPIRE key milliseconds [NX | XX | GT | LT]

name: PERSIST
summary: Remove the expiration from a key, making it persist indefinitely

name: KEYS
summary: Find all keys matching the given pattern (Dangerous in production)
complexity: O(N) where N is the total keys in the database
dangerReason: KEYS scans every single key in RAM and blocks the single-threaded reactor loop until completion. Use SCAN instead.

name: SCAN
summary: Incrementally iterate the keyspace cursor-by-cursor
complexity: O(1) for every call; O(N) for complete iteration

name: RANDOMKEY
summary: Return a random key from the keyspace

name: RENAME
summary: Rename a key

name: RENAMENX
summary: Rename a key, only if newkey does not exist

name: TOUCH
summary: Alters the last access time of a key(s)
complexity: O(N) where N is number of keys

name: COPY
summary: Copy a value of key to a newkey
complexity: O(N) worst case where N is size of value copied

name: OBJECT
summary: Inspect internal C++ memory representations of a key
syntax: OBJECT ENCODING | REFCOUNT | IDLETIME | FREQ key

name: MEMORY
summary: Inspect RAM consumption and diagnostics for key or server

name: PING
summary: Ping the server to verify socket connectivity

name: ECHO
summary: Echo the given string back to client

name: INFO
summary: Get information and operational statistics about the server

name: DBSIZE
summary: Return the number of keys in the currently selected database

name: SELECT
summary: Change the selected database for the current connection

name: FLUSHDB
summary: Remove all keys from the current database
complexity: O(N) where N is keys in current database
dangerReason: FLUSHDB wipes all data in the active DB. Accidental execution causes total data loss.

name: FLUSHALL
summary: Remove all keys from all databases
complexity: O(N) where N is total keys in all databases
dangerReason: FLUSHALL permanently destroys every key across all 16 databases in the cluster.

name: CONFIG
summary: Inspect and dynamically alter runtime server configurations
syntax: CONFIG GET parameter | SET parameter value | REWRITE | RESETSTAT
dangerReason: Modifying configs at runtime can change memory limits, eviction policies, or network listeners.

name: SLOWLOG
summary: Inspect slow command execution log

name: CLIENT
summary: Inspect and manage connected TCP clients
syntax: CLIENT LIST | INFO | KILL | PAUSE | SETNAME
complexity: O(N) where N is connected clients

name: MONITOR
summary: Listen for all commands received by the server in real time

name: SAVE
summary: Synchronously save the dataset to disk (binary RDB dump)
complexity: O(N) where N is number of keys in RAM
dangerReason: SAVE blocks the main server thread completely while serializing memory to disk.

name: BGSAVE
summary: Asynchronously save the dataset to disk in a background fork
dangerReason: BGSAVE triggers a process fork that may incur copy-on-write memory spike.

name: BGREWRITEAOF
summary: Asynchronously rewrite the append-only file (AOF)

name: SHUTDOWN
summary: Synchronously save data and terminate the server process
dangerReason: SHUTDOWN kills the database daemon, terminating all active client connections.

name: TIME
summary: Return the current server time in seconds and microseconds

name: COMMAND
summary: Get array of Redis command details
complexity: O(N) where N is number of commands

name: ROLE
summary: Return the replication role of the instance (master or replica)

name: MULTI
summary: Mark the start of a transaction block

name: EXEC
summary: Execute all commands issued after MULTI atomically
complexity: Depends on commands inside the transaction

name: DISCARD
summary: Discard all commands issued after MULTI
complexity: O(N) where N is queued commands

name: WATCH
summary: Watch the given keys to determine execution of the MULTI/EXEC block

name: UNWATCH
summary: Forget about all watched keys

name: PUBLISH
summary: Post a message to a channel
complexity: O(N+M) where N is subscribers and M is pattern subscribers

name: SUBSCRIBE
summary: Listen for messages published to the given channels
complexity: O(N) where N is number of channels

name: UNSUBSCRIBE
summary: Stop listening for messages posted to the given channels
complexity: O(N) where N is number of channels

name: PUBSUB
summary: Inspect the state of the Pub/Sub subsystem
complexity: O(N) where N is number of active channels

name: REPLICAOF
summary: Make the server a replica of another instance, or promote to primary
dangerReason: Connecting to a new master discards all existing keys to download fresh replica state.

name: WAIT
summary: Wait for synchronous replication acknowledgment from N replicas

name: AUTH
summary: Authenticate to the server
complexity: O(N) where N is password length

name: ACL
summary: Inspect and manage user permissions and rules
syntax: ACL LIST | USERS | WHOAMI | CAT | GETUSER username | SETUSER username rules
